transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-22 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees (Redwood): Alex Chen, Samir Patel, Lena Ortiz
Attendees (Argo Labs): Jordan Miles (CTO), Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng), Ben Torres (Platform)

Summary (auto): Quick Console tour focused on per-route cost telemetry and route-level dashboards, dive into batching and cache effects, talk about dedicated vs hosted economics and security questions. Agreed pilot next steps.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex Chen, AE at Redwood. With me is Samir, our SE, and Lena from CS. Jordan, Priya, Ben — thanks for making time. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Jordan (Argo): Good, Alex. Excited to see the console. We looked at the docs last week but want to see live breakdowns, especially on cost per route.
[00:18] Alex: Perfect. We'll do a live walkthrough of Console > Usage > Routes, show per-token cost at route level, and then Samir will jump into batching and KV cache behavior.
[00:29] Priya: Quick context — we have about 60 routes in prod, but 10 routes account for 80% of token spend. Most calls are short chat completions, some embedding for search. We host part of infra in GCP with VPC peering.
[00:44] Ben: And our SREs are nervous about sudden token spikes; we want predictable economics.
[00:49] Samir (Redwood): Totally. We'll show ways to split routing by model family and enable fallback so you can trade off latency and cost. Quick Q: are you thinking Hosted API to start or Dedicated?
[00:58] Jordan: Ideally hosted to move fast, but if economics don't make sense we may need Dedicated or private VPC. Security is big — we need SSO and KMS.
[01:07] Alex: Got it. We'll highlight security controls: SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integrations and audit logs in the Console.

-- Console walkthrough --
[01:20] Samir: Opening the console, top nav -> Usage -> Routes. Here you can filter by time range, model, and tag. We'll load last 30 days.
[01:32] Samir: On the left is a route list with average latency, tail p95, total tokens, and cost contribution. See how Route-Search is top contributor — that's consistent with what Priya said.
[01:45] Priya: Yep that's the one. Can you break down cost per request vs cost per token?
[01:50] Samir: Yeah, the chart splits token cost and infra overhead. Token cost shows model per-token unit cost, infra overhead is our execution cost — note that infra overhead is lower on Dedicated reservations.
[02:03] Ben: What's infra overhead exactly? I thought we only pay tokens.
[02:06] Alex: Good question — infra overhead is the portion Redwood bills for runtime execution (GPU hours, scheduler). On Hosted it's baked into per-token price but visible here so you can see where batching or caching reduces it.
[02:19] Jordan: Do you show per-model quantization or optimized kernel differences in the cost?
[02:23] Samir: We tag model variants (e.g., gptx-quant8) and show relative token cost. The console recommends a cheaper quantized variant when quality regression is acceptable.

[02:35] Samir: Now if we click into Route-Search, you'll see a timeline of token usage, average seq length, and the cache hit rate. Cache hit rate is the KV cache prefix/caching we do — sometimes the transcript shows as K V cash in logs.
[02:50] Priya: Ha, I've seen K V cash in our notes. What's a typical hit rate improvement?
[02:54] Samir: For chat with repeated system prompts we often see 20–40% token reduction. For retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) it depends, but prefix caching of system tokens helps a lot.
[03:04] Ben: Any tradeoffs on latency if we enable more batching?
[03:07] Samir: Batching improves throughput and reduces per-token cost, but adds a small queuing latency. Console has a SLO slider per route where you can set latency targets and batching aggressiveness adapts.

[03:20] Alex: I'm going to pull up the Cost Breakdown screen. This shows token charges split by model and route, and per-route hourly burn charts so you can pinpoint spikes.
[03:30] Jordan: Can we allocate cost to teams/tags? We need to chargeback per product team.
[03:33] Samir: Yes, tag-based rollups and custom joins. You can export CSV for FinOps, or wire to our billing API.

[03:45] Priya: Security — can you show audit logs and who can see route-level data?
[03:49] Lena (CSM): Jumping in — under Settings -> Security you can see SSO config, role definitions, and audit logs. Audit logs include request metadata, not PII, and KMS handles key management for private deployments.
[04:02] Jordan: Do you support customer-managed keys / HSM?
[04:05] Lena: Yes, for Private deployments we support KMS and HSM integrations; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS as an option on enterprise plans.

-- Pilot & economics discussion --
[04:18] Alex: For a pilot, common approach is a 2-week baseline using your sample routes. We instrument with per-route tracing and run a small traffic replay. That gives projected monthly spend and expected gains from batching/caching.
[04:31] Jordan: Sounds good. What's a realistic delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
[04:35] Samir: Depends on steady-state throughput. If you have sustained high qps on a few routes, Dedicated with reserved GPUs plus quantized models can cut token-equivalent spend by 25–45% after batching and cache gains.
[04:48] Ben: If we go dedicated, how disruptive is migration?
[04:51] Alex: Not disruptive — same API and routing. You can pin routes to Dedicated capacity in the Console, and we do canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks to Hosted if capacity is constrained.
[05:03] Priya: What about region residency — we need EU-only data.
[05:06] Lena: We have Private (VPC) deployments in EU regions and can support VPC peering for Hosted traffic routing. We'll include region-specific controls in the security pack.

[05:18] Jordan: A couple of product-y questions: can we do A/B routing per route for model variants?
[05:22] Samir: Yes, canary/A-B is built-in. You specify traffic percents, and Console shows per-variant quality metrics side-by-side. If the new variant degrades, auto-fallback triggers.
[05:33] Priya: How do you measure quality regressions in the Console?
[05:36] Samir: You can attach evaluation prompt sets to routes; Console runs basic evals and throws alerts on quality regressions (BLEU/ROUGE or custom heuristics). We also integrate with customers' eval infra via webhook.

-- Pricing nuance & objections --
[05:48] Jordan: Pricing — our procurement will push for predictable unit costs. Do you have committed-reservation pricing?
[05:53] Alex: Yes, Redwood Dedicated comes with reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual) and lower per-token-like unit economics. For hosted, we give volume discounts and quantization recommendations that reduce unit costs.
[06:04] Ben: Any hidden costs during spikes?
[06:07] Alex: We have burst capacity with configurable policies. Console shows projected overage and alerts; you can set hard caps to avoid surprise charges.

[06:15] Priya: Who typically owns the pilot? Our infra team or product?
[06:19] Alex: Usually a cross-functional owner — platform + ML eng. For onboarding Redwood provides a short runbook and Samir will help with the traffic replay.

-- Quick perf dive by Samir --
[06:30] Samir: For the perf checklist, we want sequence length distribution, average tokens per request, P95 latency targets, and a representative payload sample. That drives kernel selection and batching profiles.
[06:42] Priya: We'll send that. Also interested in the console metric that shows "effective token cost after batching" — is that shown?
[06:49] Samir: Yep, it's the effective unit in the Route view; it shows before/after when you toggle batching and cache suggestions. There's also a simulation mode to project savings if you enable suggestions.

[07:02] Jordan: Competitors — you mentioned others earlier. How do you compare with OpenAI or Anthropic for cost predictability?
[07:08] Alex: We're focused on serving/runtime economics and observability. Unlike direct model APIs, Redwood adds batching, KV prefix caching, routing and dedicated capacity controls — so you get more levers to optimize. We'll share a short competitor comparison doc.

[07:22] Ben: Ops question — if we want logs exported to our Splunk/Datadog, is that possible?
[07:25] Samir: Yes, event sinks for telemetry, plus per-request traces you can forward.

[07:32] Priya: Any gotchas with embeddings? We use Pinecone for indexing — embeddings cost is a big line item.
[07:38] Samir: Embedding calls are charged per embedding unit but same console shows embedding-level spend. We can recommend batching embeddings or switching to lower-cost embedding models where quality allows.

-- Closing and recap --
[07:50] Alex: Quick recap: Redwood will send pricing + security docs; Samir will share perf checklist; Argo to provide route sample and traffic csv; Lena will schedule pilot kickoff. Pilot scope: 2 weeks traffic replay, analyze per-route savings and latency impact, aim to quantify savings and recommend next step (Hosted pilot extension or Dedicated sizing).
[08:12] Jordan: That works. One ask — can you include an example SOW for a proof-of-concept?
[08:16] Lena: Yes, we'll attach a short SOW template and pilot success metrics.
[08:20] Priya: Also please include the evaluation webhook docs so we can hook our internal evals.
[08:26] Samir: Will include that.
[08:29] Ben: Timeline — we can provide route csv by Wednesday, ready to start pilot the following week.
[08:33] Alex: Great. We'll follow up via email with the materials and proposed kickoff slots. Thanks everyone.
[08:38] Jordan: Thanks all, good demo.

Auto-generated Questions (may be partial):
- What is expected savings moving to Dedicated given our route distribution?
- How does KV cache impact repeated system prompt workloads?
- Can we export per-route cost to our FinOps stack?

End of transcript.
